title: CCA-1.1 Destabilizes MYC proteins to induce irreversible anti-proliferative effects in hepatocellular carcinoma.
authors: Utomo, Rohmad Yudi; Hapsari, Novia Permata; Nugraheni, Nadzifa; Lestari, Beni; Hanifa, Mila; Linda Laksmiani, Ni Putu; Zulfin, Ummi Maryam; Muto, Daisuke; Ikawati, Muthi; Suenaga, Yusuke; Hippo, Yoshitaka; Meiyanto, Edy; Jenie, Riris Istighfari
one_liner_zh: 该文研究CCA-1.1化合物通过抑制EGFR信号和促进MYC蛋白降解来抑制肝癌增殖，虽含分子对接和MD模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与TF-DNA课题关联较弱。
abstract: N-Myc and c-Myc, as two major members of the MYC family proteins, independently contribute to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) by promoting proliferation, survival, and metabolic reprogramming. Overexpression of both proteins correlates with poor clinical outcomes, while intrinsic structural disorder hinder direct pharmacological targeting of MYC proteins. CCA-1.1 exhibits enhanced biological and physicochemical properties over its parent compound, curcumin, and demonstrates potent anti-cancer activity in various cancer types. We aim to investigate the anti-proliferative activity of CCA-1.1 through modulation of the MYC proteins and induction of cell cycle arrest and/or cell death mechanisms, including senescence, apoptosis, and autophagy. CCA-1.1 exhibited potent and irreversible anti-proliferative activity on Huh-6 cells by inhibiting EGFR kinase activity and its downstream signalling. CCA-1.1 also promoted G2/M arrest, induced apoptosis, and generated senescence. At the molecular level, CCA-1.1 downregulated N-Myc and c-Myc protein levels through the promotion of GSK3beta activation and suppression of NCYM, a stabilizer protein of N-Myc. Furthermore, CCA-1.1 activated autophagy as a result of MYC protein destabilization. CCA-1.1 exerts a multi-faceted anti-cancer effect in MYCN-expressed HCC cells by inhibiting kinase signalling and destabilizing MYC proteins, leading to apoptosis, senescence, and autophagy. Molecular docking and molecular dynamic simulation revealed that CCA-1.1 interacted with both N-Myc and c-Myc. Our findings demonstrate CCA-1.1 as a distinctive anti-cancer candidate for HCC driven by MYC activation.
abstract_zh: N-Myc和c-Myc作为MYC家族蛋白的两个主要成员，通过促进增殖、存活和代谢重编程，独立地促进肝细胞癌（HCC）的发生。这两种蛋白的过表达与不良临床结局相关，而内在的结构无序性阻碍了直接靶向MYC蛋白的药理学干预。CCA-1.1相较于其母体化合物姜黄素，表现出增强的生物学和理化性质，并在多种癌症类型中展现出强效的抗癌活性。我们旨在研究CCA-1.1通过调节MYC蛋白及诱导细胞周期阻滞和/或细胞死亡机制（包括衰老、凋亡和自噬）的抗增殖活性。CCA-1.1通过抑制EGFR激酶活性及其下游信号传导，对Huh-6细胞表现出强效且不可逆的抗增殖活性。CCA-1.1还促进了G2/M期阻滞，诱导凋亡，并产生衰老。在分子水平上，CCA-1.1通过促进GSK3beta激活和抑制NCYM（N-Myc的稳定蛋白）来下调N-Myc和c-Myc蛋白水平。此外，CCA-1.1因MYC蛋白去稳定化而激活自噬。CCA-1.1通过抑制激酶信号传导和去稳定化MYC蛋白，在表达MYCN的HCC细胞中发挥多方面的抗癌效应，导致凋亡、衰老和自噬。分子对接和分子动力学模拟揭示，CCA-1.1与N-Myc和c-Myc均发生相互作用。我们的发现表明，CCA-1.1是针对MYC激活驱动的HCC的一种独特抗癌候选药物。
